notes:
POC + pricing negotiation summary:
- Customer: OpalWell (mid-market SaaS analytics). Primary contact: Head of Product (Jules Park). Eng lead: Marco Diaz.
- Timeline: started exploring Hosted API (Jan), small hosted POC (2 weeks) -> moved to Dedicated POC (Feb) after latency/cost concerns.
- Hosted POC findings: stable integration via SDK, average token cost OK, but variability in p95 latency during spikes (seen 220-280ms p95 on large chat workloads). Team quoted: \"need sub-200ms p95 for chat feature to ship\".
- Dedicated POC (2-week): deployed 2 reserved instances (equiv. A100 x2 profile). Benchmarks: p50 ~ 65-80ms, p95 ~ 140-160ms for short-chat (<=256 tokens), throughput ~40-55 requests/sec across the pool. KV prefix caching showed ~18-22% token reduction on support dialogues.
- Quality: internal evals against sample prompts show parity with hosted models; minor regressions on rare domain-specific phrases (tracking for eval set).
- Cost profile: team modelled 3 commit options: 6-mo / 12-mo / 24-mo. Preferred economic target: blended unit cost reduction of ~30% vs hosted at steady-state.
- Negotiation points currently open: commit level (we proposed 2 GPU committed baseline), burst capacity policy (burst to 4 GPUs for up to 12 hours/day), ramp schedule (start 50% commit month1 -> 100% month3), overage pricing formula (customer wants predictable per-token cap rather than % uplift).
- Specific ask from OpalWell: show example SOW with ramp schedule + a 3-month trial at reduced commit (they want to lock infrastructure for Q3 product launch). Also require invoice/contract to include data residency clause + KMS key custody options.
- Security: SSO/SAML + SOC2 required; they asked for audit log retention 12 months and region (us-east) residency.
- Quotes from calls: \"If we can't get predictable cost for launch we won't be able to commit\" — Jules Park (Head of Product).
- Links: pricing deck (see drive link), security FAQ (drive). POC tickets: INFR-239 (kernel perf), POC-512 (KV cache tuning).
- Internal red flags: legal flagged data residency language (needs to be explicit), finance needs ARR banding for procurement (we submitted estimate 75k-250k ARR).

Sales notes / playbook suggestions:
- Offer 3-tier commit: 
  1) Pilot (3 mo): 50% committed capacity, limited burst (1.5x), higher overage cap per token to protect Redwood.
  2) Standard (12 mo): 100% committed baseline, burst up to 2x sustained with 30 hours/month included, overage at negotiated flat per-token rate.
  3) Enterprise (24 mo): 100% commit + guaranteed burst to 4x for launch windows, built-in ramp schedule and lower overage.
- Proposed numbers (starting point for AE): baseline reserved pool equivalent to 2x A100 = $18k/mo commit, burst buffer add-on $6k/mo (or pay-as-you-go bursts at 1.8x), overage floor $0.00015 per token with a cap at $X/month (customer wants firm cap; legal to confirm).
- Concessions to consider to close faster: 3-month pilot at 60% discount on commit fee, include 2 launch-day burst credits, deadline: must sign SOW by 2026-04-10 to guarantee Q3 capacity.
- SE action: validate updated perf matrix for 4x burst mode (Ravi). Provide detailed overage calc spreadsheet to finance (Ravi + Lila).
- Next internal: prepare SOW template with ramp table + data residency appendix; coordinate legal.
